solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Domestic meal cooked by retired English ruler once

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a domestic cleaner

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been worked over, so these letters are rearranged
retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A cleaner prepares a meal for an elderly Englishman who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' looks like an adjective for the meal; it is the cleaning woman, a char.
explanation.definitionFit: The Frankish king crowned emperor in 800 is a ruler of long ago, hence the 'once'.

clue.text: Animal briefly in river

parts.note: in, meaning fashionable, is hip
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A creature glimpsed for a moment in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday shortening of hippopotamus, so a short form of an animal's name.

clue.text: Comedian from long ago, endlessly raised roof, we hear

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards
endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: of yore means from long ago, so yore stands for it

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word's sound, not its spelling, is wanted

parts.note: a hood is a roof, as on a car or pram

explanation.surface: A veteran comic is remembered for bringing the house down, someone reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts YORE to YOR, which 'raised' turns into ROY.
explanation.definitionFit: Roy Hudd was a long-serving British comic and music-hall entertainer, known for radio's The News Huddlines.

clue.text: Being part of hospital, computer systems close to capacity

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
IT, information technology, covers computer systems

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so take the end of the next word

explanation.surface: Hospital computers are nearly overloaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is anything that exists in its own right, which is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: A relative taking heartless Irish idiot personally

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a relative

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter is removed

parts.note: eejit is Irish (and Scottish) slang for an idiot

explanation.surface: A family member takes a foolish Irishman's remarks to heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces one's own view, the same as saying 'speaking personally' or in my opinion.

clue.text: Country's revolutionary top-class graduate in scrap

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or top-class, its 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: to bin is to scrap or throw away
an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A rebel's best student lands in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Top-class is A1, its 1 standing for the letter I; 'revolutionary' turns the whole string round.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a nation in south-west Africa, so it fits as an example of a country.

clue.text: Christopher, with companion, cleanses soiled culinary equipment

parts.note: Kit is a short form of Christopher
CH stands for Companion of Honour

indicators.note: soiled, meaning messed up, tells us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: Christopher and a friend wash some dirty kitchen gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Scales for weighing ingredients are a standard piece of cooking apparatus.

clue.text: Roll in the NAAFI maybe sounding so lean

indicators.note: sounding signals that a word's sound, not its spelling, is wanted

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus
to list is to lean, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A bread roll at the forces canteen seems thin.
explanation.walkthrough: The NAAFI runs canteens and shops for British forces; a roll there could be a register, such as the list of those off duty ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a list of names, and this one records service personnel too unwell for duty.

clue.text: Dish, as informed later, that may contain eggs

indicators.note: later places the following pieces after the one that defines the nest

parts.note: a bird's nest is a place that may hold eggs
so can mean as, in 'so far' and 'as far'
to be up on something is to be informed about it

explanation.surface: A recipe, as you will be told later, may include eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese delicacy made from swiftlet nests, served as a course at a meal.

clue.text: Express indirectly spotted when heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: pimply skin is spotted

explanation.surface: Hinting at something you noticed as you were leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply something is to suggest it without stating it outright.

clue.text: Chaps in office win no local runs (among seven)

indicators.note: no means without, so the abbreviation is removed

parts.note: a triumph is a win
the local is the pub, PH (public house) on maps

indicators.note: among signals one piece placed within another

parts.note: VII is seven in Roman numerals
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Officials take power, though the local team scores nothing among the seven.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the three men who shared power in ancient Rome, a plural noun for office-holders.

clue.text: Game, with outside of the ball getting a battering

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game played with mallets and balls

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: During a game of croquet the ball gets a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battering' is not a beating: the ball is coated in batter or crumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a small rissole of food, coated and fried, so a ball given a coating.

clue.text: Such a King Edward could get black edging

definitions.text: Such a King Edward could get black edging

indicators.note: edging puts the black at the front edge of the other pieces

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
K is the chess abbreviation for king
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A King Edward potato cooked in the oven may get charred skin.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato variety; one cooked in its jacket can blacken at the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Oven-cooked jacket potatoes are often King Edwards, so the whole clue describes one.

clue.text: Key event containing upmarket foreign brass, as it were

indicators.note: containing signals one piece holding another inside

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
a do is a party or event
U means upper-class or upmarket

explanation.surface: An important occasion featuring top foreign officers, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' looks like top officers; here it is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was Portugal's currency, and brass is slang for money, so it is foreign cash.

clue.text: Unemotional type, that's often won at fete, caught for good

indicators.note: caught for good means one letter replaces the other

parts.note: a goldfish in a bag is a classic prize at a fair
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A prize from the village fair, landed for keeps.
explanation.walkthrough: A fete is a British outdoor fundraising fair with stalls and games.
explanation.definitionFit: A person described this way is aloof and lacks feeling, an idiom for an unemotional character.

clue.text: Hobby-horse, needing repair at top, rejected

parts.note: to fix is to repair

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: top means number one, written NO 1, the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A rocking horse that needs mending at its head is cast aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Top is No 1, written NO plus the figure 1 read as I; 'rejected' sends it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby-horse is a pet topic one keeps returning to, an obsession.

clue.text: Continue showing old king in newspapers, etc

indicators.note: in signals pieces placed within another

parts.note: the press is newspapers and other news media
GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: The papers keep running stories on an elderly monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To progress is to go forward or proceed, which is to continue.

clue.text: Seamen ordered fast food without hesitation in European city

indicators.note: ordered here suggests a spoken order, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: salts, as in old salts, are seamen

indicators.note: without here means going without, so the hesitation sound is dropped from the food word

parts.note: a burger is fast food
er is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: Sailors order a quick meal without dithering on a trip to a city in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Salzburg is the Austrian city of Mozart's birth, so a city in Europe.

clue.text: Hound The Eagles in outskirts of Belgrade?

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed within another
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: ernes are sea eagles

explanation.surface: Birds of prey stalk the edges of the Serbian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bernese mountain dog is a breed of dog, loosely a hound.

clue.text: Gets married, gets divorced, essentially having to cut back

indicators.note: essentially points at the core of the word, and cut back says that core is turned round

parts.note: a couple who divorce untie the knot

explanation.surface: Someone weds, splits, and essentially has to retrench.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle letters TI of UNTIES are turned round, giving IT.
explanation.definitionFit: When two people marry they join together, so they combine as one couple.

clue.text: Perhaps a stage for daring entertainment that's on hand

definitions.text: Perhaps a stage for daring entertainment
definitions.meaning: a fakir's bed of spikes is a platform for a daring act
the skin beneath a fingernail lies on the hand

explanation.surface: A daredevil performance stage that's ready and waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Read one way it is a bed of nails for a stunt; read the other it is the tissue under a fingernail.

clue.text: Noise from, say, silver jackfish when separated

indicators.note: when separated tells us to break the single word jackfish into its two halves and clue each one

parts.note: the first half, jack, is abbreviated as on playing cards
the second half, fish, as a verb means to try to catch with rod and line

explanation.surface: A silvery fish makes a sound when pulled apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silver' looks like the fish's colour, but it is loose change whose clinking is the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose coins clinking together make a metallic ringing, the sound silver change gives.

clue.text: On the subject of retracting, Mayor of Salford bottles up

indicators.note: retracting means drawing back, so the letters are read backwards
bottles up means the letters are held inside these words

explanation.surface: A northern town's mayor backtracks and keeps things to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Both introduce a topic, as in 'regarding' or 'concerning'.

clue.text: Youngster, ten, probing slug that's damaged plant

indicators.note: probing means poking inside, so these pieces go within
damaged signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a lad is a youngster
IO resembles 10, ten

explanation.surface: A boy pokes at a slug that has been eating a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' turns SLUG into G...US around LADIO.
explanation.definitionFit: The gladiolus is a flowering garden plant with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: I'm amused about openings in young advertising firm

indicators.note: about means going round other letters

parts.note: LOL, laugh out loud, is text shorthand for amusement

indicators.note: openings are first letters

explanation.surface: A pleased boss looks over the new ad agency.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm friend is one who is staunch and faithful.

clue.text: In spring, one's presented with course before going on vacation

parts.note: a course can be a direction, such as east
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, so only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: In spring a person receives a course of study before heading off on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate gifts are handed out at the spring festival, so one is something given then.

clue.text: Parking area over by university that's swamped in US

parts.note: a bay is a parking space
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A car park next to a campus flooded in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow marshy creek in the southern states, i.e. a waterlogged place in America.

clue.text: News about line dancing? The leader to get beer and cheese

indicators.note: about means stirred around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ley is a ley line, a supposed straight line between ancient sites

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: A report on a line dance; the dance leader gets a beer and some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Wensleydale is a crumbly cheese from a Yorkshire valley.
